title: a CRLF was copied with length 3 into a buffer whose guard only promised room for 2
object: the connection write buffer, one direct malloc of wsize bytes
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a guard that reserves N bytes while the copy that follows writes N+1
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct malloc/calloc/realloc, with neither slabs.c nor cache.c between it and the request.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: 1.6.45:memcached.c carries `memcpy(resp->wbuf + len, "\r\n", 2);` (`grep -c` = 1). The length-3 form is at 49f3b0ca9b57^ and is absent from the pin. A fix-reversal.

nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from the platform allocator with no inner layer between -- this is not a slab chunk and not a cache.c object -- so under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the guard and the copy disagree by exactly the string's NUL: `len + 2 > wsize` reserves room for the CR and the LF, and `memcpy(..., "\r\n", 3)` writes a third byte. So the crossing happens only at the exact boundary len + 2 == wsize, which is why it survived -- and it is one of TWO instances the same earlier commit planted.
